title: InventoryItem
description: A row of the user's food inventory. PERSISTED. Source of record: DinnerDecider/Models/InventoryItem.swift:50-92. Note: on iOS this is a SwiftData @Model class, NOT Codable, so there is no shipped JSON encoding of it. This schema describes the persisted field set field-for-field so a port's store (Room, SQLite, JSON file) stays compatible. TODO(unresolved): the canonical cross-platform wire encoding for `dateAdded`. No JSON encoding of InventoryItem exists in the Swift (searched Models/, Services/, and the Kroger export path), so RFC 3339 date-time below is this document's recommendation, not an extraction.

name.description: Item name. Half of the merge key.

brand.description: Brand, or null. The other half of the merge key: two rows with the same name but different brands are DISTINCT items.

categoryRaw.description: The category stored as a RAW STRING, deliberately, so the store keeps a stable value even if the enum is reordered or renamed later (InventoryItem.swift:54). The typed `category` accessor maps it through FoodCategory and falls back to `.other` for anything unrecognized; the setter writes back rawValue. Ports must persist the string, never an ordinal.

quantity.description: How many of this item are on hand. Merged on confirm (duplicate keys stack) and decremented by 1 per use when a recipe is cooked. A row reaching 0 is flagged for removal. See shared/pipeline/scan-pipeline.md.

dateAdded.description: When the row was created. Defaults to now. Drives the `dateAdded` inventory sort option.

sourcePhotoID.description: Identifier of the photo this item came from, or null for manual entry.

isStaple.description: A staple the user almost always has (salt, oil). Shown collapsed so it does not clutter the main list. MUST default to false: the Swift declares `var isStaple: Bool = false` specifically to keep SwiftData lightweight migration happy for stores written before the field existed (InventoryItem.swift:59-62). A port adding this field to an existing store must default it the same way.

$comment: The merge key is NOT a stored field: it is computed as trim(lowercase(name)) + "|" + trim(lowercase(brand ?? "")) - InventoryLogic.mergeKey, InventoryLogic.swift:12-16. The name-only key used to match recipe ingredients is trim(lowercase(name)) - InventoryLogic.nameKey, InventoryLogic.swift:20-22. Both must be reproduced exactly; InventoryLogicTests pins the pipe separator via literals such as "milk|horizon" and "eggs|".
